analysis.summary: Useful original recovery leads exist, especially the small native focus routines and managed input-repeat logic. No corresponding recovery was found by name/address searches in recovered C++ or the native registry. Original SHA-256 matches the note. No behavior tests were executed.
corrections: setFocus(-1) is not a demonstrated clear-focus API: the native integer overload forwards the ID into recursive tree selection without a sentinel check.
changeSelection uses the SSP overload of elUIScreen.setFocus, not the cited integer overload.
updateVisibility is stateful: it calls gaMenuReel.tick and updates child positions; treating it as a pure visibility refresh would omit original side effects.
Wraparound is an intentional extension. The note's synthetic tests and reported observation-only live test establish neither faithful recovery nor safety of the abandoned action prototype.

findings.hint: Recover this compact recursive tree-selection routine first. ABI is x86 thiscall: ECX=this, one stack integer, boolean result in AL, callee pops four bytes. Body spans 0x448180–0x4481FB; padding precedes the next entry at 0x448200.
evidence: Original objdump shows gates on byte +0x174 bits 2 and 4, with byte +0x190 providing an alternate eligibility path.
Compares requested ID with +8; on a match, checks state +0x10 against 3 and may invoke vtable +0x54 with arguments 1 and -1.
Traverses four-byte child entries between +0x178 and +0x17C, recursively calling 0x448180 and stopping on success.
Returns occur at 0x4481A1, 0x4481C1, 0x4481F0 and 0x4481F9; the first return is not the routine boundary.
No corresponding name/address entry was found in searched recovered sources or native_blocks.hpp.
dependencies: Child vector and item lifetime invariants
Virtual callback at vtable +0x54 and its side effects
validation_plan: Compare against original execution using valid item trees covering every eligibility gate, matching root, matching child, absent ID and duplicate IDs.
Record callback order, arguments, return AL and state mutations.
Include -1 as an ordinary ID, both present and absent.
limits: Virtual callback implementation was not inspected.
No original execution or differential harness was run.

findings.hint: Recover the small screen wrapper with exact SSP ownership semantics. ECX=this and one stack integer; body ends at 0x48F618 exclusive, followed by padding and a separate entry at 0x48F620.
evidence: Calls 0x448180 on screen +0x0C with the supplied ID, then calls 0x447E90 with a temporary SSP output address.

Compares the returned pointer with screen +0x14; replacement decrements the old object's +4 reference count, conditionally invokes its deleting destructor, stores the new pointer and increments its count.
Releases the temporary SSP before ret 4 at 0x48F615.
Original SEH registration references 0x8FF408.
No corresponding recovery or native registry entry was found by searched names/addresses.
dependencies: SSP reference counting and virtual deleting destructor
validation_plan: Compare original and recovered wrapper with unchanged focus, changed focus, absent ID and ID -1.
Record screen +0x14, reference counts, destructor calls and tree callback effects.
Recover the complete 0x447E90 routine before relying on absent-ID behavior.
limits: Only the beginning of 0x447E90 was disassembled; its complete boundary and null-result conditions remain unresolved.
The wrapper ignores the selection routine's boolean result; this alone does not establish whether focus clears.

findings.hint: Recover the complete method, prioritizing its input-repeat state machine as a separable behavioral unit. Preserve boolean return semantics and all non-navigation actions.
evidence: Method table row 4181 identifies tickInput. Original header bytes encode a 12-byte header and 763 code bytes; actual IL ends with returns at IL_02F8 and IL_02FA.
IL_0047–0079 subtracts gaTimer.dt from float +380 using double intermediates and clamps through an unordered-aware branch.
Direction +376 is latched as -1 or +1, with the -1 input taking precedence when initially choosing direction.
IL_0164 and IL_01CE call changeSelection; each accepted call is followed unconditionally by copying float +384 into +380.
IL_0259–02B2 decreases +384 by dt times 0.070000000298023224, clamps to approximately 0.02, or resets it to 0.25.
The remainder includes overlay dismissal, a virtual action with argument 3, and A–Z jumpToSelection polling.
dependencies: Input-manager singleton and device virtual calls
validation_plan: Trace original input callback results and replay fresh presses, holds, releases, simultaneous directions and direction changes.
Compare +376/+380/+384, selection-call order and boolean return across frames.
Include countdown boundaries, period clamp, alphabet jumps and non-navigation actions; preserve IL floating-point conversion and unordered-branch behavior.
limits: Input calli signatures and target implementations were not fully resolved.

review.summary: Approved as assembly-reference evidence only for VA 0x448180–0x4481FB inclusive (124 bytes). The first return is an eligibility failure, not the function boundary; four padding bytes separate the last return from the next entry at 0x448200. The ID -1 has no special handling in this routine, so it is not established as a clear-focus sentinel. Byte equality provides no recovered-source credit.
review.reason: Independent disassembly confirms the complete control flow, thiscall ABI, recursive call, virtual callback, and stated boundaries. Assembling and linking the symbolic candidate at its original VA produced an exact, unmasked 124-byte match against Game.exe; the original and candidate hashes also match the receipts. The child-vector and lifetime invariants and virtual callback behavior remain external dependencies, and no original execution or source-equivalence test was performed.
